time.PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TI.provenance: MEASURED on the live 16.402 effects stream (every projectile object on every frame of the captures): the princess tower's arrow (TowerPrincessProjectile Speed 600) advances 599-600 native per tick on 293 consecutive steps of capture 20260920-003751-B and 688 of 20260920-081819-B, the king tower's (Speed 1000) 999-1000, the Musketeer's (Speed 1000) 1000, the Bomber's (Speed 400) 399-400, the Cannon's (Speed 500) 499-500 -- one projectile Speed unit is one native millitile per 50 ms tick, the troop unit (18 subtiles), not 15. History: hypothesis 15 (2026-09-13) mirrored a 'tiles/min at 20 TPS' reading; the AesDragon wiki blog's assertion and the Darknighture frame test (x1.2 for both a Musketeer projectile and a Giant) were right.

history.provenance: Mirrors time.SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK (Speed = tiles/min at 20 TPS). Community: the AesDragon wiki blog ASSERTS (unmeasured) that projectile Speed uses the troop unit; a Darknighture frame test (2023) measured x1.2 (Speed/50) for BOTH a Musketeer projectile and a Giant. No source was found for a 'troops /50, projectiles /60' split. crforge and legacy/ use /60 for both. Kept as its own key so a recording can split projectiles from troops without a code change (docs/spell-spec.md, projectile and rolling families).
